Get Optimal Transition Matrix

get_optimal_transition_matrix.Rd

Compute the optimal cell transition matrix by integrating node-pair depth information with per-cell annotations. The function: (1) filters to terminal (single-leaf) cells of selected cell types, (2) calls calculate_transition_matrix() to infer the best transition matrix under structural constraints, (3) flattens that matrix into a long data frame of start/end cell-type pairs with normalized transition strengths, and (4) labels results with the evaluated depth cutoff.

This version is Windows-safe: all internal parallelism is automatically coerced to single-core on Windows so that vignette building (pkgdown) will not fail with 'mc.cores' > 1 is not supported on Windows.

Usage

get_optimal_transition_matrix(
  node_pair_depth,
  cell_info,
  Sel_u,
  fi_depth,
  Bound_Matrix,
  cell_type_list,
  mc.cores = parallel::detectCores()
)

Arguments

node_pair_depth

A data frame containing node pair depth information (e.g. from calculate_lca_depths()).

cell_info

A data frame with per-cell info; must contain at least cellNum and celltype. Only rows with cellNum == 1 are retained (terminal leaves), and then filtered to the provided cell_type_list.

Sel_u

Character string choosing which depth/height measure to use from node_pair_depth (e.g. "lca_normalized_height").

fi_depth

Numeric. Depth cutoff / threshold passed to calculate_transition_matrix().

Bound_Matrix

Numeric matrix encoding constraints (e.g. irreversible transitions). Diagonal/upper-triangular structure often encodes prior directionality.

cell_type_list

Character vector of cell types of interest, in the order that defines the transition structure.

mc.cores

Integer. Desired parallel cores. On Windows this will be silently coerced to 1. On non-Windows it will be coerced to at least 1.

Value

A list with:

  • optimal_matrix: the inferred optimal transition matrix (cell type x cell type).

  • optimal_norm_df_dataframe: a long-form data frame with columns type_combined_new, start_cell, end_cell, norm_optimal_T, and depth ("d_<fi_depth>").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- get_optimal_transition_matrix(
  node_pair_depth   = node_pair_depth,
  cell_info         = cell_info,
  Sel_u             = "lca_normalized_height",
  fi_depth          = 0.2,
  Bound_Matrix      = Bound_Matrix,
  cell_type_list    = c("C4","C5","C6","C7","C8"),
  mc.cores          = 8
)
str(res$optimal_matrix)
head(res$optimal_norm_df_dataframe)
} # }
